children: Emyria Limited
has been selected by Compass Pathways to participate in a global late-stage clinical trial of an investigational psilocybin treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

The mental healthcare provider estimates the study could generate approximately $1.5 million in additional revenue based on 20 participants completing study activities at its Empax Centre in Leederville, Western Australia.
The agreement provides for a recruitment target of as many as 32 participants, with scope to enrol more under the study’s competitive recruitment framework.
Emyria’s national network of Empax Centres brings together psychiatrists, psychologists, and therapists specialising in the treatment of PTSD and treatment-resistant depression.
Compass is the second drug sponsor to select Emyria through its international partnership initiative, expanding a clinical trials business that operates alongside its reimbursed treatment programs.
December Recruitment Start

The Phase 2b/3 COMP202 Redefine Study aims to enrol approximately 300 adults internationally to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of Compass’s proprietary synthetic psilocybin treatment COMP360.
The randomised, double-blind controlled trial includes an open-label extension and will assess changes in PTSD symptom severity from baseline to week eight.
Under the clinical trial agreement, Emyria will handle participant screening, preparation and follow-up sessions, monitoring during dosing, safety and efficacy assessments and data entry.
Its established referral pathways and existing enquiries from potential PTSD patients are expected to support recruitment, subject to study-specific eligibility criteria.
Emyria is targeting December 2026 for the start of recruitment, subject to human research ethics committee approval and site activation.
Expanding Clinical Services Revenue

The prospective revenue from the initial 20 participants is substantial relative to Emyria’s total revenue of approximately $4.05m for the 2026 financial year, although actual trial income will depend on final recruitment numbers and completed study activities.
Compass selected the Leederville facility following a feasibility assessment and site qualification process that included a visit by the drug sponsor.

“Our specialist infrastructure, trained workforce, and experience treating real world patients within regulated healthcare settings are proving attractive to international drug sponsors,” executive chair Greg Hutchinson said.
Being selected to participate in this trial is indicative of that and an important commercial milestone—we look forward to working closely with the Compass team on this study.”
Empax Global Partnership

Emyria launched its Empax Global Partnership Program in April 2026 to provide international pharmaceutical developers with access to its specialist facilities, trained personnel, and regulatory capabilities.

By conducting sponsored research through infrastructure already established for patient care, the company aims to generate additional revenue from existing facilities and personnel while increasing utilisation and improving operating margins.

Compass is developing COMP360 for both PTSD and treatment-resistant depression, with the investigational therapy having received US Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough Therapy designation for the latter indication.
Emyria plans to continue delivering reimbursed treatment programs while pursuing further partnerships with international drug developers.

title: Emyria Selected for Participation in Compass Pathways’ Global Psilocybin PTSD Trial
